text: This is for the office move on Friday and I am too tired to explain the guest network again. Can we give the visitors their own route out through the firewall? At the moment the picture makes it look like they can wander into staff Wi-Fi. Put a pale area round the staff side and call it Internal. We also need a printer in there, connected to the switch. Leave a bit of room for the meeting room kit; I don't have the port list yet. Please keep it on one screen because this is going in the move briefing.
Switch to Firewall: both arrowheads.
The red one needs to sit between the two wireless boxes, with the grey one still above it.
No, those are two different wireless networks. You've put them so close together that it looks like one long name. Give them some space and keep their separate cables.
pls add the reception pc on left of switch and conect it. name is FrontDesk not front desk if thats important
There's nowhere on this drawing for the phones. We have six of them on the same switch, and the landlord keeps asking which bits need power.
Move the guest connection above the staff one.
okay the cable from the guest wi fi goes to the switch no sorry I mean that's what it shows now take that off and run it straight to the fire wall and write internet only beside that line
Do you know if the building's internet will actually be working by Monday?
Box round both of these, eu-west-1.
Make another region on the right. Just a standby database in that one for now.
Show replication from standby to Orders DB, other way round sorry. Primary sends to standby.
Dashed for that replication link. Under the second region put 'manual failover'.

We are still choosing a provider, so please don't turn this into a wall of AWS icons. Three plain areas is enough: public entry, application, data. Requests come in at the top, hit a load balancer, then go to two identical app instances. Each app can reach the same database. The database should be lower down, visibly inside data. Add object storage off to one side for uploads. I want to be able to point at the two app instances and say we can lose one. Could you also work out what this would cost us each month?
Rename Cache to Redis, actually keep Cache as the title and put Redis underneath in smaller writing. Procurement won't know what Redis is.
That little green square is the only thing with our customer data in it. Give it a red outline and put 'encrypted backups' underneath.

The production must stay at the right hand of the testing. Please enclose each in his own fence. The arrow between them gives a wrong idea, there is no circulation of data from testing into production.
Insert approval before Deploy.

I'm showing this to finance, so the internal job names aren't helping us. Call Build 'Package the release' and Tests 'Check it works'. After the checks we need a decision: approved for customers? Yes goes to Deploy, no goes back to Commit. Can you keep the return line underneath so it doesn't go through the words? There is also a security scan but I honestly don't know whether it runs before or after the tests. Put it beside them with a question mark for now. We can correct it when Jo wakes up.
You deleted the Tests box when I asked you to remove the connection. Put the box back between Build and Deploy. I only wanted that direct route to deployment gone.
The step immediately before the green one needs an owner: Release captain.
A failed test seems to lead to exactly the same place as a passed one here. That's going to be an awkward slide at the audit.
rollback shoud go back to last good relase not all way to commit. can u fix arrow only
Finally, that makes sense. I'll paste it into the release notes after lunch.
Make staging like production.
Start with Idle and Running. start takes Idle to Running.
Running can go to Paused on pause. resume goes back.
stop from either active state returns to Idle. Keep those lines outside the triangle.
Paused is still blue. I asked for both active states to be orange, including the one that's waiting.

The firmware folks and the app folks are using 'connected' to mean different things, which is why I'm drawing this. We start Disconnected. A connect request takes us to Connecting; a successful handshake takes us to Ready. Don't call that state Connected. If the handshake times out, we go back to Disconnected. Once Ready, a lost connection sends us to Retrying, and a successful retry goes to Ready again. After three failures we give up and go to Disconnected. Put the three-failure condition on the arrow rather than making another state for it. I may be missing a cancellation path. Leave that as a note beside Connecting so we remember to ask.
The arrow marked 'expire' should go from Locked to Open—no, that's exactly backwards. Open to Locked on expire.
and after the timeout
Can you get from the one at the bottom back to Idle without passing through Error?

This is the account screen for the demo, not the finished design. Please move Save changes under the fields and line up its left edge with theirs. We need a small 'Forgot password?' link beside the password field. Under Email address, add a note saying we'll send a verification message if they change it. The header has loads of dead space; make it shallower. I don't want to spend the whole afternoon choosing colours, blue is fine. Could we have a second version alongside this showing an invalid email, with the error message actually below that field? Keep the first version so I can show the difference.
Save button wider.
Put the two input boxes a little closer together. Leave the blue button where it is.

text: Why is 'Forgot password?' a giant box? It's just a link. Lose the border and make it look like a line of text under Password.

Cancel belongs on the left in our app. Can the red button trade places with it?
These actions are the reverse of the rest of the product. Put the destructive action where the grey one is now, and shift the grey one into the space it leaves. Same row, same styling.

I'm the manager on call this weekend and this flow assumes a lot of knowledge I don't have. Between the alert and the impact question, put a step to open the status dashboard. Beside it, leave room for the link; I will paste that later. If there is impact, paging the lead is right, but we should also start an incident log. Those two things can happen together. The watch-for-ten-minutes route needs to come back to the impact check, otherwise the person just sits there forever. Please make the wording big enough to read on a laptop at 3 am.
Watch for 10 min → Watch for 5 min.
if db red dont restart it!! add call DBA before that restart box pls
There's a long way from 'page incident lead' to the actual phone number. It would be nice to have the number right there, even if it's only a placeholder until we check it.
Change the escalation timer to fifteen minutes. Sorry, that's weekdays; make it five minutes and put 'weekends' next to it.
